SDK Project Scaffold Creation:
Develop a project scaffold for each Software Development Kit (SDK) to establish a structured foundation for further development.
Configuration of Code Generation Tooling:
Configure code generation tooling using OpenAPI specifications to automate the generation of code for each SDK.
CI Pipeline Setup for Automated Code Generation:
Establish a Continuous Integration (CI) pipeline to automate code generation, ensuring that the development workflow is smooth and efficient. Continuous Integration (CI) is a development practice that involves automatically integrating code changes into a shared repository. This process helps detect and address integration issues early in development, enhancing code stability and supporting collaborative workflows. The CI pipeline ensures that code generation occurs seamlessly, contributing to efficient and error-free development.
ms.criteria:
Enhancing Access to SDK Code:
Create and manage open and user-friendly repositories for each SDK, containing all the necessary foundational code.
Host these repositories within the txpipe community on GitHub at https://github.com/txpipe.
Clearly define the names of the repositories as they are decided upon during the development process.

Streamlining Code Generation Process:
Establish a structured process that seamlessly generates the required code from OpenAPI specifications.
Ensure that this process is well-organized to handle code generation efficiently for each SDK repository.

ms.report:
We are pleased to announce the successful completion of Milestone #2 for the Marlowe Runtime SDKs Catalyst project. We are proud of the aggregation of the progress made during Milestone #1 and #2 and truly excited to show off the new features to get feedback from the community.
Milestone goals and proofs of completion
Develop User-Friendly Wrappers for RUST and Go:
Build user-friendly layers for RUST and Go on top of automatically generated code.
Rust: Some parts of the automatically generated code were modified to handle the headers of the Marlowe Runtime REST API and some parts of the responses were hidden as well because they were only needed if you didn’t use the SDK. https://github.com/marlowe-contrib/marlowe-rust-sdk/blob/main/src/lib.rs 
Go: Here the automatically generated code was good enough to be considered a fully functional SDK. Some parts of the SDK were modified to reach a level of functionality that was missing. https://github.com/marlowe-contrib/marlowe-go-sdk/blob/main/api_default.go 
Include essential explanations within the code for better understanding.
Rust: We kept the automatically generated docs and added manual comments in the manually generated code.
https://github.com/marlowe-contrib/marlowe-rust-sdk/blob/main/src/lib.rs
https://github.com/marlowe-contrib/marlowe-rust-sdk/blob/main/marlowe_client/docs/DefaultApi.md
https://github.com/marlowe-contrib/marlowe-rust-sdk/tree/main/marlowe_client/docs 
Go: We kept the automatically generated docs as they were good enough to show the usage of the SDK.
https://github.com/marlowe-contrib/marlowe-go-sdk/blob/main/api_default.go
https://github.com/marlowe-contrib/marlowe-go-sdk/blob/main/docs/DefaultAPI.md
Incorporate tests to ensure smooth integration and functionality: For both languages only getters have automatic testing. All of them are manually tested to ensure quality. This decision was made because transaction signing in each language is a job that exceeds the scope of this project.
